text:
harper: Customer is seeing streaming dropouts ~28-32s into the SSE response. Logs show request_id=rtx-9a2f and a short 200 then EOF. Need a reproducible curl + exact capture steps we can ask the customer to run.

samir: ok. main goals: preserve chunking (no buffering), capture headers, capture raw bytes, and include verbose TLS/proxy trace. keep it minimal.

maya: short curl I'd ask them to run (replace $TOKEN and $URL):

```bash
TOKEN=REDACTED
URL="https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-small&stream=true"

# dump headers to stdout, raw output, no buffering, http2, and write an ascii trace
curl -N -v -D - \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \
  -H \"Connection: keep-alive\" \
  --http2 \
  --trace-ascii /tmp/curl-trace.txt \
  --trace-time \
  --max-time 120 \
  "$URL" 2>&1 | tee /tmp/stream-output.txt

# Notes: -N disables buffering so chunk boundaries are preserved. -D - prints response headers. --trace-ascii captures lower-level socket/TLS details. tee both captures for upload.
```

samir: also ask them to run a version against our LB directly (if they can reach it) and with their proxy to see differences. example for proxy: add `--proxy http://<proxy_host>:<port>` and `-U user:pass` if needed.

zane: to capture request ids on the wire include this extra header echo (our infra copies X-Request-Id):

```bash
# include a client-side id so we can correlate if their stack rewrites headers
curl -N -v -D - -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"X-Client-Request: local-rtx-9a2f\" \"$URL\"
```

maya: when they run it, ask for these artifacts: /tmp/stream-output.txt, /tmp/curl-trace.txt, and the exact curl command they used (redact token). Also ask if they're behind a corporate proxy or using a mobile carrier.

harper: can we provide a tiny checklist for support to paste to customer so it's copy/paste friendly?

samir: yes, condensed checklist: 1) Run the exact curl above (replace token & url). 2) Save both trace and output. 3) If behind proxy, re-run with --proxy and attach both. 4) Include the log timestamp and the request_id from our service (rtx-9a2f). 5) Upload files to the debug bundle link we give.

support-bot: debug-bundle upload endpoint: https://files.redwood.ai/upload?case=rtx-9a2f — please attach /tmp/stream-output.txt and /tmp/curl-trace.txt.

zane: one more tip — if the customer can reproduce locally, run `stdbuf -oL` (on some shells) in front of curl to force line buffering in the pipeline: `stdbuf -oL curl ... | tee out.txt`. helps prevent our terminal from rebuffering.

maya: i validated the curl locally (no proxy) and got a sustained stream >2m with no EOF using -N + --trace-ascii. with a simple corporate proxy it truncated at ~30s — looks like an intermediary timeout. pls ask customer to test proxy/no-proxy and share traces.

harper: perfect. i'll paste the copy/paste checklist into the ticket and request uploads. thanks all :thumbsup:

support-bot: reminder: tag the case with `streaming-interruption` and `curl-repro` so eng gets alerted.
